items.title: Chink Martin Interview, 1966-10-19
items.q: You had the biggest bands I did before. Well, Isen Jones and way back.

ctx.x: Well, what you don't like now is the boy and the girl stand clear across the room from each other.

But don't let nobody kid you. They don't let nobody kid you or nobody else. That's something that you can't teach nobody. It's got to come. It's got to be born in you. That's all the story. But for all, it's like plenty of them, you know, the critics are talking about the colored man playing more rhythm and playing strictly tempo than the white. No, don't let nobody kid you. That's been my life. You had the biggest bands I did before. Well, Isen Jones and way back. Like that. Okay. Now that big, there was no…

I always felt sorry for the bass player in some of these modern jazz bands because he's the only one that's keeping the tempo. The drummer is playing strictly counterpoint, making bombs bursting in air.
